mechanism_narrative: The four-week accelerating decline in RETAIL_REC (-19.4 to -26.3) reflects a persistent downward momentum in overall mobility that will continue without reversal over the next four weeks absent an external shock.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the past 28 days despite three or more consecutive weeks of prior decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in WORKPLACES mobility below -20% removes incidental retail visits tied to commuting routines, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining below the -20 threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate a compounding reduction in both commuting and discretionary travel capacity; their joint suppression of mobility drives RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks more than either series alone would predict.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue declining together.

mechanism_narrative: Synchronized week-over-week declines across RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES are consistent with renewed public caution during a case-wave regime (e.g., a summer COVID resurgence), prompting voluntary avoidance of retail venues that persists for the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: three or more categories decline simultaneously for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds upward despite continued synchronized decline across all four categories, or the inferred case-wave regime does not materialize.

mechanism_narrative: The mid-July timing coincides with peak summer heat and vacation season, during which residents travel away from the metro area or avoid outdoor retail activity during the hottest hours, producing a short-term further dip in RETAIL_REC over the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2022-07-15 falls in peak summer season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises within the next week despite the ongoing summer season, indicating the seasonal mechanism is not dominant.

mechanism_narrative: Declining GROCERY_PHARM alongside a rising RESIDENTIAL index suggests households are consolidating errands and spending more time at home, a behavioral shift that reduces discretionary retail trips captured in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks even as GROCERY_PHARM continues falling and RESIDENTIAL continues rising.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in PARKS exceeding 8 percentage points, as observed between t-1w and t-0w, signals a broader pullback from outdoor leisure activity that typically precedes a parallel pullback in retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 8 points within a single week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -8.7 to -17.9 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within two weeks following a PARKS drop exceeding 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: If local authorities reinstate advisories or capacity guidance in response to rising case trends, indirectly reflected by concurrent sharp drops in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, retail footfall will show an immediate one-week further contraction before any stabilization.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next week despite concurrent TRANSIT and WORKPLACES declines exceeding 3 points.
